title: The steam car
subject: reading

paragraphs.text: The successes and failures of the Doble brothers and their steam cars

When primitive automobiles first began to appear in the 1800s, their engines were based on steam power. Steam had already enjoyed a long and successful career in the railways, so it was only natural that the technology evolved into a miniaturized version which was separate from the trains. But these early cars inherited steam’s weaknesses along with its strengths. The boilers had to be lit by hand, and they required about twenty minutes to build up pressure before they could be driven. Furthermore, their water reservoirs only lasted for about thirty miles before needing replenishment. Despite such shortcomings, these newly designed self-propelled carriages offered quick transportation, and by the early 1900s it was not uncommon to see such machines shuttling wealthy citizens around town.

But the glory days of steam cars were few. A new technology called the Internal Combustion Engine soon appeared, which offered the ability to drive down the road just moments after starting up. At first, these noisy gasoline cars were unpopular because they were more complicated to operate and they had difficult hand-crank starters, which were known to break arms when the engines backfired. But in 1912 General Motors introduced the electric starter, and over the following few years steam power was gradually phased out.

Even as the market was declining, four brothers made one last effort to rekindle the technology. Between 1906 and 1909, while still attending high school, Abner Doble and his three brothers built their first steam car in their parents’ basement. It comprised parts taken from a wrecked early steam car but reconfigured to drive an engine of their own design. Though it did not run well, the Doble brothers went on to build a second and third prototype in the following years. Though the Doble boys’ third prototype, nicknamed the Model B, still lacked the convenience of an internal combustion engine, it drew the attention of automobile trade magazines due to its numerous improvements over previous steam cars. The Model B proved to be superior to gasoline automobiles in many ways. Its high-pressure steam drove the engine pistons in virtual silence, in contrast to clattering gas engines which emitted the aroma of burned hydrocarbons. Perhaps most impressively, the Model B was amazingly swift. It could accelerate from zero to sixty miles per hour in just fifteen seconds, a feat described as ‘remarkable acceleration’ by Automobile magazine in 1914.

The following year Abner Doble drove the Model B from Massachusetts to Detroit in order to seek investment in his automobile design, which he used to open the General Engineering Company. He and his brothers immediately began working on the Model C, which was intended to expand upon the innovations of the Model B. The brothers added features such as a key-based ignition in the cabin, eliminating the need for the operator to manually

ignite the boiler. With these enhancements, the Dobles’ new car company promised a steam vehicle which would provide all of the convenience of a gasoline car, but with much greater speed, much simpler driving controls, and a virtually silent powerplant. By the following April, the General Engineering Company had received 5,390 deposits for Doble Detroits, which were scheduled for delivery in early 1918.

Later that year Abner Doble delivered unhappy news to those eagerly awaiting the delivery of their modern new cars. Those buyers who received the handful of completed cars complained that the vehicles were sluggish and erratic, sometimes going in reverse when they should go forward. The new engine design, though innovative, was still plagued with serious glitches.

The brothers made one final attempt to produce a viable steam automobile. In early 1924, the Doble brothers shipped a Model E to New York City to be road-tested by the Automobile Club of America. After sitting overnight in freezing temperatures, the car was pushed out into the road and left to sit for over an hour in the frosty morning air. At the turn of the key, the boiler lit and reached its operating pressure inside of forty seconds. As they drove the test vehicle further, they found that its evenly distributed weight lent it surprisingly good handling, even though it was so heavy. As the new Doble steamer was further developed and tested, its maximum speed was pushed to over a hundred miles per hour, and it achieved about fifteen miles per gallon of kerosene with negligible emissions.

Sadly, the Dobles’ brilliant steam car never was a financial success. Priced at around $18,000 in 1924, it was popular only among the very wealthy. Plus, it is said that no two Model Es were quite the same, because Abner Doble tinkered endlessly with the design. By the time the company folded in 1931, fewer than fifty of the amazing Model E steam cars had been produced. For his whole career, until his death in 1961, Abner Doble remained adamant that steam-powered automobiles were at least equal to gasoline cars, if not superior. Given the evidence, he may have been right. Many of the Model E Dobles which have survived are still in good working condition, some having been driven over half a million miles with only normal maintenance. Astonishingly, an unmodified Doble Model E runs clean enough to pass the emissions laws in California today, and they are pretty strict. It is true that the technology poses some difficult problems, but you cannot help but wonder how efficient a steam car might be with the benefit of modern materials and computers. Under the current pressure to improve automotive performance and reduce emissions, it is not unthinkable that the steam car may rise again.

Questions 14–20

Reading Passage 2 has seven paragraphs, A–G.

Choose the correct heading for each paragraph from the list of headings below

questions.explanation:
14. 本题最主要的大意提示在A段的第二和第三句话里。在此之前的第一句相当于交代背景引出主题：汽车的雏形基于蒸汽引擎。紧接着，第二句话称赞蒸汽技术在此前很长一段时间里成果斐然，这对应了good aspects。第三句话则开门见山地指出：然而基于蒸汽技术的小汽车也同时继承了这种技术的缺点，这则对应了bad aspects。接下来的第四和第五句，分别举例说明了到底是哪些方面存在缺陷。最后一句则又绕了回来，说“虽然蒸汽车有着诸多缺点，但还是有优点并被广泛使用着”。综合全段的文意，相当于在好处和坏处之前来回跳跃、公正持中地综合点评了蒸汽技术，清晰地对应了正确选项：iii。

15. 本段篇幅不长，开篇第一句就言简意赅地定了基调：蒸汽车的好日子并不长。有着良好预测能力的考生，读到了这里应该就能大致领悟接下来的文意走向：必然是有了更好的取代者导致其没落。果不其然，第二句话点出“内燃机技术的出现促成了汽油车的面世”，第三和第四句话用先抑后扬的方式描述“一开始汽油车缺点多多，但是后来进行了改良，导致蒸汽车逐渐退场”。虽然段落中并没有使用任何可以直接同义替换题干better option的词汇，但结合全段意思却不难看出，表达的正是“汽油车是个比蒸汽车更好的选择”这个意思。考生只要不是执着于非要找到词汇的对应，就不难顺利锁定正确选项：viii。

Questions 21–23

Choose the correct letter, A, B, C or D.

questions.prompt: What point does the writer make about the steam car in Paragraph B?

options.text: Its success was short-lived.
Not enough cars were made.
Car companies found them hard to sell.
People found them hard to drive.

questions.explanation:
这种问“某一段作者提出了什么看法”的问题，优点和缺点都非常明显。优点是完全不用耗费任何时间去定位，缺点则是基本无法指望靠只看段落中的某一句两句话而得出总体结论。不过本段对于考生解题还是相对比较友好的，因为如前文分析第15题时所说，本段一共只包含了四句话，且第一句话说“蒸汽车的好日子不长”其实就已经对应到了正确答案，只不过谨慎的考生当然还是看完全段、综合了解全部内容之后再笃定作答为好。本题答案为A项：Its success was short-lived.（它的成功期很短暂。）

B项：Not enough cars were made.（没有生产出足够的车辆。）如果只单看B段的话，那么其实并没有提及任何关于蒸汽车生产数量的信息；如果考生的记性不错，对A段内容仍有印象的话，甚至可能觉得这个题干的表述与A段最后一句话“经常看到这些机器承载富有市民来来去去”（说明数量不算很少）有些矛盾。

C项：Car companies found them hard to sell.（汽车公司发现它们很难卖得出去。）如果说上一个选项好歹还与文章内容有一些相关性的话，本选项则完全是没有在文中被提到过的、风马牛不相及的内容。假如这是一道判断题，那么本项就是一个妥妥的NOT GIVEN项。

D项：People found them hard to drive.（人们发现它们很难开。）考生只要看懂了本段的第三句话，就不难看出“操作更复杂”（也就是更难开）这个特点是用来定性使用内燃机的汽油车而非蒸汽车的，因此，本项其实与原文形成了矛盾抵触，不是正确答案。

questions.prompt: When building their first steam car, the Doble brothers

options.text: constructed all the parts themselves.
made written notes at each stage of the construction.
needed several attempts to achieve a competitive model.
sought the advice of experienced people in the car industry.

questions.explanation:
本题虽然看似定位简单，但其实是“一头披着羊皮的恶狼”，考法凶残。之所以看似定位简单，是因为题干中的大写Doble brothers和first steam car这两条线索，都一模一样地出现在了C段的第二句话里。之所以考法凶残，是因为本题实际上需要考生看完长长的一段、反复对比四个选项后，运用排除法将另外三个要么与段中某句信息相矛盾抵触、要么根本没有在段中被提及过的信息都排除掉，才能准确得出答案为C项：needed several attempts to achieve a competitive model.（需要做出若干次尝试以获得一辆优质的车型。）

这个正确答案的得出，需要考生结合C段从第二句话开始直到几乎是全段结束的地方，才能综合提炼出“他们几经尝试、不断改良，这才终于让他们设计的蒸汽车型有了许多优点”这个意思。这几乎相当于又做了一道问全文大意的List of Headings题目。不过，采用平行阅读策略的考生应该会轻松得多：由于是在兼顾所有题型、逐步推进解题动作，所以虽然前文中的第16题和此处的第22题都要求读一遍很长的C段，但很显然考生只需要阅读一次、凭借尚且新鲜的记忆同时解答这两道题就可以了。

A项：constructed all the parts themselves.（自行制造了所有的零部件。）C段的第三句话里说到，他们制造第一辆车的时候使用了从一辆破烂且年代久远的蒸汽车上拆下来的零件，这个信息与本选项形成了鲜明直接的矛盾抵触。

B项：made written notes at each stage of the construction.（在生产制造的每一个阶段都做了笔记记录。）这个选项完全不曾在C段中出现过，看遍段意后要排除它就应该并不困难，主要的困难在于考生需要耐心地去看遍段意。

D项：sought the advice of experienced people in the car industry.（寻求了汽车行业内有经验人士的建议。）这个选项与上一项类似，也是段落中完全没有提到过的信息。

questions.prompt: In order to produce the Model C, the Doble brothers

options.text: moved production to a different city.
raised financial capital.
employed an additional worker.
abandoned their earlier designs.

questions.explanation:
本题很好地奖励了采用平行阅读策略的考生，惩罚了只想靠大写信息直接定位到某一句话中就指望解题的考生。Model C这个定位线索直接出现的地方，是D段的第二句话。然而其实本段的第一句话就已经给出了“他们寻求投资并成功获得了资金开设公司”这个对应于正确答案的信息。接下来直到最后一句的段落内容，是使用了更多的细节描述来交代清楚这个车型如何进行了改良、如何比汽油车有着更多的优势之处、如何获得了顾客交付预售押金等着生产交付这样一个故事梗概。若是因为直接定位而缺失了对第一句话的阅读，则反而欲速不达，错失更早遇见正确答案的机会。答案为B项：raised financial capital.（筹措了资金资本。）

A项：moved production to a different city.（将生产制造搬到了另一个城市。）本项的干扰混淆性其实非常弱。D段首句确实说到了Abner Doble从一个城市去了另一个城市，但他驾驶的是Model B而非Model C，且去另一个城的目的也是为了谋求投资而非批量生产。考生只要阅读时稍加留心，应该就不难做出区分。

C项：employed an additional worker.（雇佣了一个额外的员工。）这条信息完全不曾在原文中被提及过。

D项：abandoned their earlier designs.（抛弃了他们先前的种种设计。）在使用Model C直接定位到的D段第二句话里，明确说到了Model C是在Model B各种创新设计的基础上进一步拓展放大，这与选项表述是直接的矛盾抵触。

groups.contextHtml:
The Model E


The Model E was road-tested in 1924 by the Automobile Club of America. They found it easy to drive, despite its weight, and it impressed the spectators. A later version of the Model E raised its [24] ______ , while keeping its emissions extremely low.
The steam car was too expensive for many people and its design was constantly being altered. Under [25] ______ cars were produced before the company went out of business. However, even today, there are Model Es on the road in the US. They are straightforward to maintain, and they satisfy California’s  [26] ______ emissions laws. Perhaps today’s technology and materials would help us revive the steam car.

articleHtml:
The steam car
The successes and failures of the Doble brothers and their steam cars


A

1[14] ______

 When primitive automobiles first began to appear in the 1800s, their engines were based on steam power. Steam had already enjoyed a long and successful career in the railways, so it was only natural that the technology evolved into a miniaturized version which was separate from the trains. But these early cars inherited steam’s weaknesses along with its strengths. The boilers had to be lit by hand, and they required about twenty minutes to build up pressure before they could be driven. Furthermore, their water reservoirs only lasted for about thirty miles before needing replenishment. Despite such shortcomings, these newly designed self-propelled carriages offered quick transportation, and by the early 1900s it was not uncommon to see such machines shuttling wealthy citizens around town.
B 2[15] ______
But the glory days of steam cars were few. A new technology called the Internal Combustion Engine soon appeared, which offered the ability to drive down the road just moments after starting up. At first, these noisy gasoline cars were unpopular because they were more complicated to operate and they had difficult hand-crank starters, which were known to break arms when the engines backfired. But in 1912 General Motors introduced the electric starter, and over the following few years steam power was gradually phased out.
C 3[16] ______
Even as the market was declining, four brothers made one last effort to rekindle the technology. Between 1906 and 1909, while still attending high school, Abner Doble and his three brothers built their first steam car in their parents’ basement. It comprised parts taken from a wrecked early steam car but reconfigured to drive an engine of their own design. Though it did not run well, the Doble brothers went on to build a second and third prototype in the following years. Though the Doble boys’ third prototype, nicknamed the Model B, still lacked the convenience of an internal combustion engine, it drew the attention of automobile trade magazines due to its numerous improvements over previous steam cars. The Model B proved to be superior to gasoline automobiles in many ways. Its high-pressure steam drove the engine pistons in virtual silence, in contrast to clattering gas engines which emitted the aroma of burned hydrocarbons. Perhaps most impressively, the Model B was amazingly swift. It could accelerate from zero to sixty miles per hour in just fifteen seconds, a feat described as ‘remarkable acceleration’ by Automobile magazine in 1914.
D 4[17] ______
The following year Abner Doble drove the Model B from Massachusetts to Detroit in order to seek investment in his automobile design, which he used to open the General Engineering Company. He and his brothers immediately began working on the Model C, which was intended to expand upon the innovations of the Model B. The brothers added features such as a key-based ignition in the cabin, eliminating the need for the operator to manually 
ignite the boiler. With these enhancements, the Dobles’ new car company promised a steam vehicle which would provide all of the convenience of a gasoline car, but with much greater speed, much simpler driving controls, and a virtually silent powerplant. By the following April, the General Engineering Company had received 5,390 deposits for Doble Detroits, which were scheduled for delivery in early 1918.
E 5[18] ______
Later that year Abner Doble delivered unhappy news to those eagerly awaiting the delivery of their modern new cars. Those buyers who received the handful of completed cars complained that the vehicles were sluggish and erratic, sometimes going in reverse when they should go forward. The new engine design, though innovative, was still plagued with serious glitches.
F 6[19] ______
The brothers made one final attempt to produce a viable steam automobile. In early 1924, the Doble brothers shipped a Model E to New York City to be road-tested by the Automobile Club of America. After sitting overnight in freezing temperatures, the car was pushed out into the road and left to sit for over an hour in the frosty morning air. At the turn of the key, the boiler lit and reached its operating pressure inside of forty seconds. As they drove the test vehicle further, they found that its evenly distributed weight lent it surprisingly good handling, even though it was so heavy. As the new Doble steamer was further developed and tested, its maximum speed was pushed to over a hundred miles per hour, and it achieved about fifteen miles per gallon of kerosene with negligible emissions.
G 7[20] ______
Sadly, the Dobles’ brilliant steam car never was a financial success. Priced at around $18,000 in 1924, it was popular only among the very wealthy. Plus, it is said that no two Model Es were quite the same, because Abner Doble tinkered endlessly with the design. By the time the company folded in 1931, fewer than fifty of the amazing Model E steam cars had been produced. For his whole career, until his death in 1961, Abner Doble remained adamant that steam-powered automobiles were at least equal to gasoline cars, if not superior. Given the evidence, he may have been right. Many of the Model E Dobles which have survived are still in good working condition, some having been driven over half a million miles with only normal maintenance. Astonishingly, an unmodified Doble Model E runs clean enough to pass the emissions laws in California today, and they are pretty strict. It is true that the technology poses some difficult problems, but you cannot help but wonder how efficient a steam car might be with the benefit of modern materials and computers. Under the current pressure to improve automotive performance and reduce emissions, it is not unthinkable that the steam car may rise again.
